divergence: Measured on a bare extruded body, uncut by the envelope: massv2 rotate removes 0 m3 (displace) acting on 2 volume(s) (multiple). The BOOK records this word as displace on multiple volumes. The two agree on both counts, so the second implementation is a restatement rather than a different word - it may still differ in proportion, which this bench does not measure.

mathematical_basis.reference: Affine transform: a 4x4 homogeneous matrix, invertible, straight lines preserved
mathematical_basis.definition: An orthogonal 4x4 with determinant 1 about a stated pivot. Volume and shape are exactly preserved; only bearing changes.

delivery_contract.why: A unary AST chain, a decompose() != 1 refusal inside every macro, and a maximum_components=1 promotion gate. The reason is written in candidate_analysis.py: a detached piece is no more architectural than a small Lego speck, and split wings or arrays must be joined by an explicit bridge or spine.
delivery_contract.note: So the BOOK record's `multiple` means how many volumes the operative involves, NOT how many bodies come back.

volume_law_finding.verdict: defect - the code disagrees with its own docstring
volume_law_finding.explanation: The docstring says 'rotate one partitioned bar about the pair's shared edge (BOOK p.23)'. The shared edge runs along the longitudinal axis, so rotating about it needs rotation_axis = longitudinal_axis. The code picks the remaining axis instead - a rotation in plan about a POINT of the edge - and puts the pivot at the far end of the partition line, so a positive angle drags the moving bar diagonally across the retained one. The union then absorbs the overlap: intersection area 82.37 by shoelace, 658.9 m3, union 1395.5 on 1920 = -27.3%.
volume_law_finding.severity_note: Part of the size is a tie-break, not the defect. At label 1/1 the weighted centre is exactly 0.5, so base_volume_contract.py:97-103 falls through to a hard-coded +1.0 outward sign, which puts the pivot at the far end. With -1 the same angle swings the bar away and the union comes out LARGER than the host. A 3/8 or 1/4 sentence resolves that sign on real evidence.
volume_law_finding.basis: box 20x12x8 under a 1/1 long_axis book_base_volume scope

outcome.what_changed: The hinge opens instead of closing into the bar it is hinged to. The angle magnitude is still the author's; its sign is now taken from the geometry - the swing that carries the related bar away from its partner is the one used. -27.3% became +6.7%.
outcome.residual: The remaining +6.7% is the hinge pad, not lost or gained material: each bar is grown by 3.5% of the transverse span so they overlap when flat, and once they swing apart that double count stops cancelling. Both bars are rigid throughout - this is an accounting fact about the union, and the pad is what keeps the pair one connected body.
